To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) NADPH oxidase 4 (Nox4) is a major source of ROS in the cytosol and mitochondria; (2) Nox4 is regulated by the phosphorylation of the N-terminal proline-rich domain by Src family kinases and protein kinase C; (3) Nox4-mediated ROS generation regulates the activation of Src family kinases, which are important for the regulation of cell proliferation, survival, and migration.
Reactive oxygen species (H2O(2)) are generated in the cell by the action of membrane-associated NADPH oxidase (Nox) and cytoplasmic NADH oxidase (Ndufv2) in response to growth factor stimulation.
ROS are produced by diverse mechanisms and are involved in a wide variety of cellular signaling pathways.

how cells control the generation of ROS and the role of ROS in the regulation of intracellular signaling pathways.

ROS are not simply byproducts of aerobic life, but rather they are involved in a variety of cellular processes including cell growth, differentiation, apoptosis, and immune responses.
ROS are not only byproducts of aerobic metabolism, but are also signaling mediators in a variety of cellular processes.
